title: Shopping Trip
paragraphs: “Looks like the transformation will still take some time. Should I cook something? I’ll check the market and see if I can find anything cheap.”
“You’re willing to cook, Naofumi?”

“Well, last night’s ‘grilled meat’ was really just stone grilling and using the armor Motoyasu brought as an impromptu iron plate. I’ll pick up some proper cooking equipment while I’m at it,” Father sighed.
“Alright then, we’ll… ugh, I feel awful…”
Ren and Itsuki suddenly swayed and had to lean against the carriage.
“Did you guys forget you were still seasick? Or maybe you’ve gotten used to it enough to momentarily forget?”
“What should we do?”
“Éclair still hasn’t fully recovered from the seasickness either… Let’s have Motoyasu use his healing magic on them first.”
“That won’t fix the root problem.”

At best, magic can only ease the symptoms. Same goes for motion sickness medicine—it only helps mitigate the effects. Still, it should get them moving again. But the fact that it doesn’t cure the sickness makes it a bit of a hassle.
“Motoyasu, take Ren and the others to their rooms. I’ll take Sakura and the rest of the Filolials to the riverside. After that, we’ll go shopping.”
“Understood!”
I cast healing magic on Ren and the others to get them back on their feet, then helped them to their rooms at the inn. Father guided the Filolials to the river and returned shortly after.
“Alright, let’s go shopping. Let me know if anything’s poisonous. I still haven’t learned many skills, so I can’t tell yet.”
“Got it!”
We followed Father to the market. Since this town never sleeps, all sorts of things were being sold.
“Some of these ingredients look really ominous. I guess this is just normal for demi-humans?” Father muttered as he stared at some eyeball-like vegetables hanging from a stall.

At another stall, there were… what looked like small drawstring pouches? I glanced back and forth between a cucumber-like vegetable and the pouch. Next to them, there was something resembling dried abalone.
Could it be that those are what’s inside the pouches?
“Try not to let your mind wander to anything indecent.”
Father suddenly scolded me, as if he had sensed something. Indecent? What’s indecent about this?
“I don’t understand.”
That being said, Father seemed pretty accustomed to this country’s cuisine last time. I, on the other hand, have no clue how to prepare these ingredients.
“How do you even cook this?”
“Hm?”

When Father asked, the shopkeeper gave him a suspicious look. To diffuse the tension, Father casually pointed at the ingredients. Nothing seemed wrong with that approach. Perhaps humans were just rare around here, so the shopkeeper was naturally wary.
“My weapon is a shield. Shields are great, aren’t they? They protect people.”
Father suddenly declared this, raising his shield. It seemed to be his way of signaling that he meant no harm. Surprisingly, the shopkeeper’s attitude softened a little.
“Ah, so this is your first time seeing these ingredients?”
“Yes, I ended up in Siltvelt due to some circumstances, and I wanted to learn more about the local cuisine. I’m also a big fan of The Legend of the Shield Hero.”

Father smoothly weaved in the information I had told him earlier, skillfully guiding the conversation. I remained silent, observing his negotiation skills. No matter how many times I loop through this, no one outperforms Father when it comes to negotiations. The shopkeeper stared at Father’s shield, likely assessing its condition. Of course, since it’s a Legendary Shield, it doesn’t require maintenance. In fact, it’s far superior to any ordinary shield. Eventually, the shopkeeper seemed satisfied and resumed the conversation. He looked to be in a slightly better mood.
“Hmm… Alright. Normally, I wouldn’t give humans a discount, but I can tell you take good care of your shield. I’ll throw in a discount and teach you how to prepare this.”
“Thank you.”
“For this one, you have to cut it open with a blade like this, split it apart, and scoop out the insides.”
Saying this, the shopkeeper demonstrated how to prepare the abalone-like ingredient, which turned out to be a fruit.
“L-Like this?”
“You need to use more force, or it won’t split properly.”
Father seemed a bit hesitant due to its shape. But… what even is this strange food?
“Hah!”

With a spirited shout, Father added more force to his cut, precisely splitting the fruit along its seam. Relying on his instincts, he then neatly extracted the flesh, even though the shopkeeper hadn’t given him any instructions yet.
“The fibers seem to make peeling it a bit tricky.”
“You’re pretty skilled, huh? Alright, then try this one.”

The shopkeeper continued explaining the peculiarities of the different ingredients. Finally, there was the drawstring pouch-like one—it turned out to be a fruit as well. Apparently, the seeds inside were the tasty part.
“If I crack this open, it’ll probably give off a strong smell, so I’ll do it later.”
“Fair enough.”
It seemed Father had already figured out how to handle and prepare the ingredients faster than the shopkeeper could explain.
“Alright, I’ll take the ones with slight blemishes. Of course—”
Father purchased a little bit of everything. Naturally, he also negotiated discounts—it was very much his style. I was the one carrying the bags.
“And I’ll take this as well.”
The shopkeeper looked at the item Father casually picked and let out an impressed sigh.
“You’ve got a good eye. You’re picking all the high-quality stuff… but at the same time, you’ve also taken some of the subpar ones that are harder to sell. Makes it hard for me to refuse.”
“Haha, is that so? Just a coincidence.”
Father acted a little sheepish, though it was clearly intentional. This was one of those cases where he adjusted his attitude to match the other person.
“What’s the most common way to cook these?”
“Grilling them over an open flame is the best. The aroma really spreads.”
“Sounds great. And… since you mixed in some lower-quality stuff, could you throw in a little extra for me?”
“Geez… fine, fine… huh?”
Tilting his head slightly, the shopkeeper accepted Father’s payment.
“Alright, let’s go, Motoyasu.”
“Understood!”
At the next stall, Father smoothly chatted with the vendor, working his way into their good graces while securing another discount.
“The stall next door sells the same thing, but their price is lower.”
“That’s because we use better-quality ingredients.”
He took a firm stance against merchants like that.
“For all that talk, it doesn’t seem to be selling well. Look, this part here has gone bad.”
“What!? Where do you see anything bad!?”
For a merchant who refused to face reality, Father simply held up the ingredient and turned towards the passersby.
“Hey, you there.”
“Huh?”

The beastman he called out to eyed him with suspicion. After all, humans had a low status here. It was like seeing a foreigner in Japan but with an even worse impression. If a human wasn’t accompanied by a beastman, the glares were even sharper.
“Is this how this ingredient is supposed to look?”
“Hmm… yeah, I think so? The ones I usually eat look like this.”
Perhaps he wanted humans to pay a higher price for lower-quality goods because he nodded along. Father hid his irritation well, but after observing him for so long, I could tell.
“Alright, I’ll buy it. But in return, you eat this part right here in front of me. It’s on me.”
“Wha—”
“There’s no problem, right? If it’s edible, then you should have no issue eating it.”
As soon as Father made a cut with his knife, a foul stench filled the air. This was completely rotten.
“You damn human—”
“Oh? So in this country, it’s normal to sell inedible food as if it’s safe to eat?”
He said it so innocently that even the surrounding people started to feel uneasy, some averting their gazes.
“Anyone else? Want to eat it?”
“Alright, alright! My bad! Just get out of here!”
“I don’t really care, but don’t you think selling something like this is a disservice to everyone here?”
“Yeah, exactly!”
The passersby took this as their chance to start berating the merchant. Many beastmen and demi-humans were hot-blooded, and they were quick to join in with jeers.
“You’re a disgrace to merchants!”
“Hey, shut the hell up!”

With rumors spreading, the merchant tried to grab Father by the collar, but he dodged effortlessly. Then, leaning in close, he whispered something in the merchant’s ear. The merchant froze, eyes widening for a moment before he stood there in stunned silence. What now?

“Well, it is a problem, but the unspoiled parts are actually quite ripe, meaning their sugar content is high. It should work well in cooking. They say food tastes best right before it spoils, after all.”
Father looked at me.
“Motoyasu, use a weak fire spell.”
“Understood!”

I conjured a small flame with Fast Fire, and Father used it to lightly roast the ingredient. Even though it had reeked of rot just moments ago, now it released a floral aroma. Passersby, drawn by the scent, gulped instinctively.
“See? This is a simple dish everyone in this country knows, right? How about it? Since it’s about to spoil and needs to be sold today, why not buy some? And right now…”
It seemed Father had already inquired about the price earlier. For reference, this shop had been selling these overripe fruits for six copper coins each.
“We’re slashing the price—only four copper coins! What do you say, everyone?”
The merchant, caught up in the momentum, quickly changed the price tag. With that, people rushed in to buy. The nearly spoiled ingredients sold out in no time.
“Alright, as promised, they’re all gone, so give me my discount.”
“…Fine.”
With a bright smile, Father secured another discount and bought more goods.
“Cooking utensils here aren’t too different from Japan’s. I think I’ve got everything I need.”
“As expected of you, Father!”
“I don’t know what you’re praising me for, but… well, that should do it. Let’s go cook by the river again.”
“Understood! Oh, by the way, Father—”
“Hmm?”
As we carried our bags and left the marketplace, I asked him,
“What did you whisper to that merchant earlier?”

“Oh, I told him, ‘If you don’t do something, this is all going to spoil, and you’ll take a loss. I’ll take care of it for you at a price that keeps you from going under. So, tell me—how much did you pay for these?’“ He murmured afterward, “It was a pretty close call, though.”
“So he knew he was about to take a huge loss?”
“Yeah. Once he realized that, he quickly accepted my offer.”
“And if it had failed?”
“Then we would’ve had to buy everything ourselves. If that happened, I planned to process it into something that could be stored longer.”

As expected of Father, he made sure he wouldn’t take a loss. He had asked the first shopkeeper about preparation methods, demonstrated it at another store, and then pushed for bulk sales to minimize losses.
Impressive. And so, we began preparing our meal.
